text:
maya: quick heads-up — seeing a spike in gRPC stalls on pod->pod streams in gpu-2 pool us-west-2, started ~10:20 UTC. 99th latency + timeouts.
ashwin: putting a monitor on it, any recent infra changes?
maya: we rolled a kernel patch to nodes last night that touched GSO/GRO offload settings and bumped kmod-net-next. also changed a CNI MTU override from 1450 -> 900 for a subset of tenants.
jules: hmm, mixed MTU in the same L2 segment can fragment. can you paste tcpdump from affected pod?
maya: sure — from app pod on node-a:
root@pod:/# tcpdump -n -i eth0 'ip[6:2] & 0x1fff != 0' -c 5 -vv
IP (tos 0x0, ttl 62, id 31785, offset 1856, flags [none], proto TCP (6), length 1514)
IP (tos 0x0, ttl 62, id 31786, offset 3372, flags [none], proto TCP (6), length 1514)

maya: the offset numbers look like fragmentation fragments.
ashwin: did ip link show on both nodes? mtu mismatch?
maya: node-a:
2: eth0: mtu 900 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000

maya: node-b:
2: eth0: mtu 1450 qdisc mq state UP ...
kai: oh no, that's a classic frag-mismatch. gRPC streaming uses larger message frames -> gets fragmented -> our kernel path + GSO changes might be dropping reassembly or hitting skb linearization issues.
jules: did you see any "IP: skb_conv" or "fragmented packet" dmesg?
maya: yes, var/log/kern.log has repeated:
[13045.123456] IPv4: bad checksum from X on eth0, l2hash mismatched
[13045.123457] IPv4: drop invalid fragment id 31785

ashwin: creating incident and short mitigation steps.
sre-bot: Incident INC-2026 created for gpu-2 east-west packet fragmentation — assigned to infra-oncall.
infra-oncall: taking this. quick mitigations: 1) revert MTU override to 1450 for affected tenants, 2) disable GRO/GSO on nodes temporarily to avoid mismatched segmentation, 3) pin the CNI version back.
maya: test rollback underway — changed CNI config for tenant-x to mtu: 1450 and restarted kubelet on node-a.
jules: also check ipfrag settings: sysctl net.ipv4.ipfrag_high_thresh & ipfrag_low_thresh; low thresh can drop too many fragments.
kai: for testing, run iperf3 with large MSS to see path behavior:
iperf3 -c <peer-pod-ip> -M 1400 -l 1200 -t 20
maya: running iperf now — getting retransmits, server reports many packet reassembly failures.
ashwin: rolling kernel revert to previous build on a single node to confirm hypothesis.
infra-oncall: also noticed RDMA cluster nodes had offload enabled — might be influencing GSO/TSO behavior. RDMA NICs sometimes bypass stack causing fragments to be handled differently.
jules: for permanent fix: ensure MTU homogenization across L2, add admission policy to detect CNI mtu conflict at pod create, and add a node-level check to compare interface MTU across routes.
kai: can we add e2e alert: if tcpdump shows >10 fragments/s across pods in a node -> page oncall?
maya: +1 — add to console alerts.
ashwin: quick status — after setting mtu back and disabling GSO on node-a the application's stream latency dropped to normal and no more stalls for 10 minutes.
maya: great. I'll coordinate a rolling fix and a postmortem.
jules: log pointers and snippets saved to incident ticket.
infra-oncall: follow-up actions: (1) patch deploy scripts to not mix mtu overrides, (2) revert kernel patch from canaries, (3) run cluster-wide mtu audit, (4) monitor RDMA offload interactions.
ashwin: thanks everyone. tagging @networking-team for deeper review :eyes: 
maya: thanks — will attach pcap to INC-2026."
